accessibility.guidelines:
- Single focus stop: the Button is one element. The visible label text and any leading/trailing icon merge into it; there is no focus order section because only one stop exists.
- The outer COMPONENT "Button" (46:2193) is a transparent wrapper around the nested Button instance (46:2187); it carries no semantics of its own and must not add a second focusable layer.
- Prefer native controls: SwiftUI Button / Material Button / HTML <button type="button">. They provide role, focusability and activation (Enter/Space on web) without custom wiring.
- The label describes the action, not the appearance. variant (default, outline, ghost, destructive, secondary, link) is purely visual; a destructive action must say so in its label text.
- variant=link still renders a button. Use an anchor (<a href>, .isLink, link semantics) only when activation navigates to a URL.
- leadingIcon / trailingIcon are decorative when a visible label is present: hide them (accessibilityHidden / contentDescription = null / aria-hidden="true").
- Icon-only sizes (icon, icon-xs, icon-sm, icon-lg) have no visible text: the label prop value must become the accessible name (accessibilityLabel / contentDescription / aria-label). An icon-only button without one is announced only as "button".
- Icon-only targets must still meet minimum touch-target size (44x44pt iOS, 48x48dp Android, 24x24 CSS px WCAG 2.5.8); expand the hit area rather than the visual size if needed.
- The Figma API exposes no disabled or loading props. If the implementation adds them, use the native disabled attribute / .notEnabled / disabled() and aria-busy respectively; they are not documented as states here.
- Do not reorder focus across states; keep the stop index stable so user gestures remain predictable.
- Do not stuff the accessible name with the hint, value, and error; each belongs on its dedicated property.
- Platform parity: iOS merges via accessibilityElement(children: .combine), Android via mergeDescendants = true, Web via the button's text content; all three expose the same single stop.

structure.generalNotes: Button is a thin wrapper COMPONENT (46:2193) around one constitutive instance of the Button component set (54:1996). The wrapper adds no padding, gap, radius or visible border (its strokeWeight 1 is configured but unpainted), so every rendered dimension comes from the embedded child. Child spacing is token-driven from the spacing/button/* family: padding-y 14, padding-x 20, gap 20. Icon boxes and glyphs share size/button/glyph/default (16), and the glyph outline uses border-width/button/icon (1.5). Default height derives from 14 + 20 (label line height) + 14 = 48. Anomalies: (1) cornerRadius 8 is hardcoded although a radius/button (8) token exists in the file. (2) Label typography is inline (Inter Medium 15/20, no text style) although typography/button/label/* tokens exist; letterSpacing was not captured by the extraction. (3) The 16 glyph box with 20 gap is a wide icon-label gap relative to the 15 label size; confirm this is intentional. No multi-mode variable collections (density/shape) exist. The primitive and semantic collections have one mode each. Known gaps: the plugin skipped the Phase I variant walk for the Button set (cross-product 48 exceeds cap 20), and the Figma MCP was unavailable for a delta. As a result, all xs, sm, lg, icon, icon-xs, icon-sm and icon-lg columns in the Button section are — (not measured), and the Variant axis (outline, ghost, destructive, secondary, link) was not measured. The file defines size-specific tokens that are probably bound in those variants (size/button/icon/{xs 28, sm 36, default 48, lg 56}, spacing/button/lg/padding-y 18, size/button/glyph/large 20, border-width/button/outline 1, typography/button/label/xs/line-height 16), but their bindings are unverified and were not used as values. summary.overview: Button is a single-element wrapper around the Button component set: its whole API (variant, size, label, leadingIcon, trailingIcon) is the child's configuration promoted to the parent. The default configuration is a hugging horizontal row of 88×48 with 14/20 padding, a 20 gap and an 8 radius, laying out an optional leading icon, the label and an optional trailing icon; variant drives fill and text color, while size sets padding and height, with the icon* sizes producing square icon-only buttons. Every configuration is one focus stop with a button role whose accessible name comes from the label, and icon-only sizes need an explicit accessible name. Only the default variant and size were measured, so the other variants and sizes still need re-extraction to be fully specified.
